name: MiniMud
english_description: A genuine pre-LDMud, Amylaar-driver-era testbed skeleton -- only 19 files (7 commands, one room, one player class, master + simul_efun). Not a game, a driver-feature demo: register with a bare name (no password), one starting room, look/say/who/ls, plus two wizard debug tools (eval -- compile and run an arbitrary LPC expression on the spot; update -- destruct and reload a single object). Zero driver_hook/set_driver_hook/H_[A-Z_]+ usage anywhere, genuinely FluffOS/MudOS-compatible. Findings: this driver's get_dir() flag value -1 (not the old Amylaar convention's 2) is needed for the detailed {filename,size,mtime} array form the archive's own log_file() needs, silently returning bare filename strings instead and crashing a size comparison; set_this_object() (used in the same function to make write_file() act with the caller's identity) was never a real efun on this driver, but is harmless to drop since the archive's own valid_write()/valid_read() unconditionally return 1 regardless of caller identity anyway; move_object()'s 2-arg classic form vs. this driver's 1-arg efun; and cat()/log_file() needing simul_efun reimplementation since neither is a real efun here. Also confirmed a piece of genuinely dead code: the master object's own process_input()/logon() functions are leftover from a driver convention where the MASTER filtered all raw player input globally -- this driver only ever calls process_input() on the INTERACTIVE object itself, so these master-level functions (including a startling 'evaluate every line of input as raw LPC' mechanism) are silently never invoked, with zero behavioral effect either way.
